subject.name_or_desc: The owner of a horse lost or stolen neer Henley (the querent, unnamed)

context.question: A horse lost or stolen neer Henley — if recoverable or not? And which way did he go?
context.setting: The horse was missing neer Henley; the querent asked both whether it was recoverable and which way it had gone.

attachments.key_positions: The lord of the twelfth, significator of the horse, retrograde and hastening to a conjunction of the lord of the querent's second house (his house of substance); the Moon locally in the second; two retrograde planets neer the cusp of the second; the sign of the twelfth and the sign wherein its lord was placed both west (the plurality of testimonies full west); the seventh house afflicted
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. XCIII: a horse lost or stolen neer Henley, if recoverable or not (printed pp.467–468)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
